# What DeeDee is for

An experiment rarely produces just one differential expression analysis (DEA): there are different treatments, time points, cell types or tissues, each with its own set of results. The questions that follow are about how these analyses relate to each other. Which genes respond in more than one contrast? Do two contrasts put the same genes at the top of their lists? Do they move genes in the same direction? 

DeeDee brings the tools to answer these questions together in one package. It is designed to be used after the DE analyses have been run and it is closely intertwined with the `DeeDeeExperiment` package: all DEAs live together in a single `DeeDeeExperiment` object (DDE), which is the input of every DeeDee function.

There are two ways to work with DeeDee:

* **Standalone functions** (`deedee_venn()`, `deedee_scatter()`, ...) that return a plot or table. They fit into scripts and reports, and are described in the [first part](#standalone-functions) of this guide.
* **A Shiny app** (`deedee_app()`) that combines all functions in an interactive interface, adds an overview of your data and a functional enrichment analysis, and can show the code behind every plot it draws. It is described in the [second part](#the-shiny-app).

# How to Install

You can install the current development version from GitHub:
```{r, eval = FALSE}
library("remotes")
remotes::install_github("lea-rothoerl/DeeDee", 
                        dependencies = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

# Example Dataset Used in this Vignette

The examples in the following chapters utilize the data from the Bioconductor package `macrophage`([Human macrophage immune response](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/data/experiment/html/macrophage.html "Bioconductor - macrophage")). The dataset comprises data from 24 RNA-seq samples of human macrophages exposed to different conditions: naive, associated with IFNg (an interferon), SL1344 (a strain of Salmonella), or both. Differential Expression Analysis was run using DESeq2, obtaining the following four contrasts: naive vs. IFNg, IFNg vs. both, naive vs. Salmonella, and Salmonella vs. both. All contrasts are woven into a DeeDeeExperiment, on which DeeDee operates.

If you're interested in how the example dataset was built, you can view the code here:

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| eval: false

library("macrophage")
library("DESeq2")
library("DeeDeeExperiment")

data("gse", package = "macrophage")
dds_macrophage <- DESeqDataSet(gse, design = ~ line + condition)
rownames(dds_macrophage) <- substr(rownames(dds_macrophage), 1, 15)

keep <- rowSums(counts(dds_macrophage) >= 10) >= 6
dds_macrophage <- dds_macrophage[keep, ]
dds_macrophage <- DESeq(dds_macrophage)

IFNg_naive <- results(dds_macrophage,
  contrast = c("condition", "IFNg", "naive"),
  lfcThreshold = 1, alpha = 0.05
)

IFNg_both <- results(dds_macrophage,
  contrast = c("condition", "IFNg_SL1344", "IFNg"),
  lfcThreshold = 1, alpha = 0.05
)

Salm_naive <- results(dds_macrophage,
  contrast = c("condition", "SL1344", "naive"),
  lfcThreshold = 1, alpha = 0.05
)

Salm_both <- results(dds_macrophage,
  contrast = c("condition", "IFNg_SL1344", "SL1344"),
  lfcThreshold = 1, alpha = 0.05
)

dde_macrophage <- DeeDeeExperiment(
  sce = dds_macrophage,
  de_results = list(
    IFNg_naive = IFNg_naive,
    IFNg_both  = IFNg_both,
    Salm_naive = Salm_naive,
    Salm_both  = Salm_both
  )
)

save(dde_macrophage, file = "data/dde_macrophage.RData", compress = "xz")
```

# What to Provide

As a part of the DeeDee universe, all functions as well as the Shiny App in this package require a *DeeDeeExperiment object* (DDE) as their primary input. For more information on DeeDeeExperiment, please refer to the [original package](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/DeeDeeExperiment.html).

Beside the DeeDeeExperiment object, each [DeeDee main function](#main-functions) takes a threshold for adjusted p-values that can be specified with the parameter `pthresh` (default = 0.05). Further, the functions have additional parameters that will be explained in the respective sections below. All functions produce colorblind-friendly output.

For our example, we use `dde_macrophage` given in the package data:

```{r, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library("DeeDee")
data(dde_macrophage, package = "DeeDee")
print(dde_macrophage)
```

# Which Function Answers which Question?

| Question | Function |
|:---------|:---------|
| Which genes are DE in several contrasts? | `deedee_venn()` (2 to 4 contrasts), `deedee_upset()` (any number), `deedee_overlap()` (the gene list itself) |
| Do two contrasts have the same genes at the top of their ranked lists? | `deedee_cat()` |
| Do the contrasts show similar distributions of logFC values? | `deedee_qq()` |
| Which genes drive the agreement or disagreement between two contrasts? | `deedee_scatter()` |
| What is the overall expression pattern across all contrasts? | `deedee_heatmap()` |
| How many genes are DE in each contrast, up and down? | `deedee_overview()` and `deedee_overview_plot()` |

\pagebreak
# Standalone Functions
## DeeDee Scatter Plot

The function `deedee_scatter()` creates a scatterplot of logFC values of the genes that are differentially expressed (adjusted p-value below `pthresh`) in both of two contrasts. If the input DeeDeeExperiment contains more than two datasets (like our example `dde_macrophage` does),  the `select1` (default = 1) and `select2` (default = 2) parameters specify which ones will be plotted (selected by list index). Genes close to the diagonal behave alike in both contrasts, genes away from it differ in the size or even the direction of their response. The points are colored by the p-value of the first (`color_by = "padj1"`, default) or the second (`"padj2"`) contrast, and the dashed lines at zero can be switched off with `ref_lines = FALSE`.

The result is an interactive plot: hovering over a point shows the gene's symbol and Ensembl ID as well as logFC and adjusted p-value in both contrasts. 

```{r scatter}
deedee_scatter(data = dde_macrophage, select1 = 2, select2 = 3, 
               color_by = "padj1", pthresh = 0.05)
```


## DeeDee Heatmap

The function `deedee_heatmap()` creates a heatmap of the logFC values for all common genes in every input dataset. The color key is given on the right side of the plot. The numeric `show_first` (default = 25) specifies the number of genes depicted (if the total number of genes is smaller, all genes are shown). The logical `show_gene_names` (default = FALSE) determines whether gene identifiers are displayed next to the heatmap, with `show_symbols` choosing between gene symbols (default) and Ensembl IDs. The logical `show_na` defines whether genes with NAs (in less than half of the contrasts) are included. The distance measure (`dist`, values: `euclidean` (default), `manhattan`, `pearson`, `spearman`) and the clustering method (`clust`, values: `single`, `complete`, `average` (default), `centroid`) can be chosen as well. 

```{r heatmap}
deedee_heatmap(data = dde_macrophage, show_first = 25, show_gene_names = FALSE, 
               dist = "manhattan", clust = "centroid", show_na = FALSE, 
               pthresh = 0.05)
```

The heatmap is produced with the [InteractiveComplexHeatmap](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/InteractiveComplexHeatmap.html) package. A Shiny window with the heatmap and its interactivity can be opened by running `InteractiveComplexHeatmap::ht_shiny(res)` on a result `res` of `deedee_heatmap()`. For more information, please refer to the [InteractiveComplexHeatmap Vignette](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/InteractiveComplexHeatmap/inst/doc/InteractiveComplexHeatmap.html).


## DeeDee Venn Diagram

The function `deedee_venn()` creates a Venn diagram depicting the overlaps of differentially expressed genes in the input datasets. To keep the Venn diagram easy on the eye, the `data` list may contain no more than four datasets. To compare more DEAs in a similar, set-based manner, please make use of [`deedee_upSet()`](#deedee-upset-plot). The parameter `mode` can be set to `up`, `down`, or `both` (default), specifying if only up-regulated, down-regulated or both DE genes will be counted. 

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
deedee_venn(data = dde_macrophage, mode = "both", pthresh = 0.05)
```


## DeeDee UpSet Plot

The function `deedee_upset()` creates an UpSet plot depicting the overlaps of differentially expressed genes in the input datasets. Contrary to [`deedee_venn()`](#deedee-venn-diagram), the UpSet plot can compare multiple (and even more than four) datasets in a visually pleasing way. The parameter `mode` can be set to `up`, `down`, `both`, or `both_colored` (default), specifying if only up-regulated, down-regulated or both DE genes shall be depicted. With `both_colored`, the plot is the same as for `both`, but the shares of the intersections in which all contrasts have positive or negative logFC values are colored according to the color key. The minimum size for an intersection to be included in the plot can be defined via the parameter `min_setsize`, default is 10.

```{r upset}
deedee_upset(data = dde_macrophage, mode = "both_colored", min_setsize = 15, 
             pthresh = 0.05)
```

## DeeDee Overlap List

While the Venn and UpSet plots show how many genes are shared, `deedee_overlap()` returns which ones: a data frame of the genes that are differentially expressed in all selected contrasts (`select`, by default all), with their symbol, and logFC and adjusted p-value in each contrast. The parameter `mode` (`up`, `down`, `both` (default)) works as for the Venn diagram. If no gene is shared by all contrasts, the result is `NULL`. The example below lists the genes behind the scatter plot above: those that are DE in both the second and the third contrast.

```{r overlap}
overlap <- deedee_overlap(data = dde_macrophage, mode = "both", 
                          pthresh = 0.05, select = c(2, 3))
head(overlap)
```

## DeeDee Q-Q Plot

The function `deedee_qq()` compares the statistical distributions of the logFC values of several contrasts against one reference contrast (`ref`, selected by position, default = 1) in a single plot, with one line per contrast. If a line follows the angle bisector (a straight line with slope 1), the two distributions are similar; deviations show where they differ, e.g. in the tails. The bisector is drawn as a reference unless `ref_line = FALSE`.

```{r qq}
deedee_qq(data = dde_macrophage, ref = 1, pthresh = 0.05)
```

## DeeDee CAT Plot

The function `deedee_cat()` creates a plot depicting Concordance At the Top curves for a reference contrast (parameter `ref`, select contrast by list index). For each contrast except the reference, a curve indicating the concordance of the top genes in the contrast's logFC-sorted gene list, against the reference's, is displayed. The argument `mode` specifies the way of sorting the genes: by highest (`up`, default), lowest (`down`) or highest absolute (`both`) logFC value. The highest rank for which the concordance is calculated is given by the `maxrank` (default = 1000) parameter. 

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
deedee_cat(data = dde_macrophage, ref = 2, maxrank = 800, pthresh = 0.05)
```

# The Shiny App

DeeDee's centerpiece is the DeeDeeApp, which provides you with an interface to interactively explore your DEA results' comparisons. It offers every plot above, an overview of the submitted data, an interactive functional enrichment analysis for genes selected in the scatter plot, table and plot downloads, and the code needed to reproduce each plot. 

## Starting the App

There are two ways to bring your data into the app: hand the DDE to the function, or call it without argument and upload the data as an RDS file on the Input tab. 

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# the DDE is given directly
deedee_app(dde_macrophage)

# or: start empty and upload an RDS file in the app
deedee_app()
```

The app opens in your default web browser. If the DDE was given in the function call, the upload field on the Input tab is collapsed, since there is nothing to upload.

## The Input tab

The Input tab shows an overview of your DDE and holds the settings that apply to all other tabs:

* **Overview of your DDE:** a table with one row per contrast, giving the tool that produced the DEA (e.g. DESeq2), the number of genes, and the number of DE genes in total, up- and down-regulated, together with a bar plot of the up- and down-regulated genes per contrast. The adjusted p-value threshold below the table defines what counts as DE here.
* **Select contrasts to use:** untick contrasts you do not want to use. They are removed from all other tabs; the overview above always shows the DDE as submitted.
* **Show gene symbols instead of Ensembl IDs:** switches the gene identifiers shown in the plots and tables.
* **Detected species:** detected automatically from the Ensembl IDs (human and mouse are supported) and used for gene links and the enrichment analysis. If the IDs are neither human nor mouse, the scatter plot and the overlap list cannot be created.

![DeeDee Input Tab](DeeDee_input_tab.png)

## The Plot tabs

The tabs are arranged in categories: **Overlap** (Venn, UpSet, Overlap List), **Concordance** (CAT, QQ), followed by **Scatter** and **Heatmap**. Each tab corresponds to a standalone function of the previous part; its parameters are set in the box on the left, and the result updates accordingly. The collapsible `INFO` panel on each tab gives a short explanation of the function and output.

Below each plot, there are two buttons next to each other:
* **Download plot (PNG)** saves the plot as an image. The switch *Include data source in downloaded image* adds a small footer to the image that names where the data comes from: the name of the uploaded file, or the name of the object that was handed to `deedee_app()`.
* **Show code** opens a window with the R code that can be used to reproduce the plot currently on screen, including all parameters as they are set, and a button to copy it to the clipboard. Please note that, in the case of an uploaded RDS file, the path needs to be adjusted since DeeDee can only see the filename, not the full system path. 

![DeeDee UpSet Tab](DeeDee_upset_tab.png)

## The Scatter Tab: from Plot to Pathway

The scatter tab holds one additional functionality:

* **Hover** over a point to see the gene's symbol, Ensembl ID, and logFC and adjusted p-value in both contrasts.
* **Click** a point to display the same details in a box below the plot, together with clickable links to the gene's NCBI or Ensembl page, depending on the identifier setting on the Input tab.
* **Select** a group of genes with the lasso or the box tool of the plot (top right) to run a functional enrichment analysis on the selected subset. Open the panel *Functional enrichment analysis on selected genes* below the plot, choose a GO ontology (Biological Process, Molecular Function or Cellular Component) and click *Run enrichment analysis*. The selected genes are tested for over-representation of GO terms with clusterProfiler, against the background of all genes tested in both contrasts. After a short runtime, the results are shown in a table, in which the GO IDs link to the respective terms, and can be downloaded as an XLSX file. 

![DeeDee Scatter Tab](DeeDee_scatter_tab.png)
